page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 vCPUs, which map to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU allocation is shared, and the instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10% at 941.59, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is similarly poor at 7.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12880.15 and a PassMark CPU score of 15708.54. Memory bandwidth is moderate, reaching 52.57 GB/sec for large block read-only operations, though the overall PassMark memory score falls into the bottom 25%. For specialized tasks, the instance handles static web serving at 12.25 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 13.62 million operations per second. Small-model LLM inference using a 135M model achieves average speeds, but performance drops significantly on medium 7B models.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the use of older Intel Xeon Broadwell-generation hardware, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require moderate multi-core capacity without demanding peak single-thread performance. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage options. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, moderate database operations, Redis caching, and multi-threaded background processing tasks that can leverage the 16 vCPUs without hitting single-core bottlenecks.
